pages.text: The Fusion Reactor is $(4)endgame power$(0): one unit dwarfs a whole reactor array, and it is also the pickiest machine you will ever build.$(br2)It burns "$(l:akaishi:plasma)plasma fuel rods$(/l)" — read the downstream fuel chain before you start.$(br2)$(bold)Two outputs:$(0)$(li)$(4)Massive akaishi energy$(0): split evenly among its energy output ports$(li)$(4)Life Ash$(0): the more you burn, the faster it banks up — a ticket to late-game life tech$(br2)Assemble the 7×7×7 onion structure on the next page first; only then will it fire.

Four onion layers anchored on the wall: outer 7×7×7 shell → 5×5×5 insulation → 3×3×3 frame → exactly 1 Fusion Core at the center.$(br2)$(bold)The controller IS a wall block:$(0) swap it in for $(4)any one shell on any outer wall$(0) — sides, top or bottom all work, corners and edges count too. The build is sized from that wall: 6 blocks deep inward, ±3 blocks along the other two axes.$(c)Fill the bottom 3 levels too$(0): no floating or buried structure.$(br2)$(bold)Layer rules:$(0)$(li)Outer shell: Fusion Shell everywhere; the controller / Energy Output / Item Input / Item Output ports may replace shell spots$(li)Insulation: all 98 spots $(4)must be Fusion Insulation$(0) — one gap voids the structure$(li)Frame cavity: the 26 spots may stay empty; insert Fuel ≤4 / Cooler ≤10 / Efficiency ≤12 frames$(li)Center: exactly 1 Fusion Core$(br2)Build it right and the controller shows $(4)formed$(0) within about a second; breaking any wrong block collapses it instantly.

$(bold)Output:$(0) each fuel slot drains energy at "rod base yield × 1.15^efficiency frames"; 12 efficiency frames reach about $(4)5.35×$(0). Produced energy splits evenly across all energy output ports (20 billion buffer each, output only).$(br2)$(bold)Temperature model:$(0) target = 50M + Σ heat value × efficiency multiplier − cooling; cooling = (Σ heat-sink efficiency% × (1 + 0.1 × cooler-frame count) + rod cooling) × 2M, where Σ only counts sinks already placed into unlocked slots on the controller's Heat page (10 max).$(br2)Heat sinks are stored in the controller: open it and drop them in/out via the Heat page; cooler frames only decide how many slots unlock and amplify cooling.$(br2)Each tick the actual temperature drifts 2% toward the target, clamped at ±2M per step — no sudden spikes.

$(bold)Sweet spot: 100M~130M, yield ×1.0$(0). Below 100M the yield slides with temperature; above 130M it decays linearly — yield bottoms out at $(e)×0.5 on the 160M theoretical peak$(0), but you never get there:$(br2)crossing $(c)159M trips the overheat shutdown$(0): burning stops, it $(bold)never explodes$(0), and it stays shut down for a forced 5-minute cooldown before it may resume.$(br2)Want full output? Pin the temperature between 100M and 130M — the yield multiplier decides how much power you squeeze from every rod.

Fusion heat sinks come in five tiers:$(li)tier1: 5%$(li)tier2: 7%$(li)tier3: 9%$(li)tier4: 12%$(li)tier5: 15%$(br2)The $(bold)Life Heat Sink$(0) (fusion_heat_sink_life) hits $(4)20%$(0) — the top grade, crafted from Life Ash.$(br2)$(bold)How to use:$(0) right-click the controller and place sinks straight into the grid on its $(2)Heat$(0) page; each Cooler Frame inside the structure unlocks one slot (10 max) and scales total cooling by (1 + 0.1 × frames).$(br2)Each sink has 8,000 durability and loses 1 every 100 ticks while running or cooling down; at zero it $(4)shatters$(0). Restock before you leave it running for days.

Burning also banks $(bold)Life Ash$(0): 1 ash per 100 billion akaishi energy consumed.$(br2)Ash is $(4)pushed out automatically$(0) through the Fusion Item Output Port — hook up an item pipe and it never clogs the core.$(br2)It is not only for heat sinks: the Life Heat Sink and the $(4)Mother Altar$(0) life tech both crave it — that is covered in "Secrets of Life". Burn enough akaishi power first.
Suggested order: start with the Energy Generator → practice heat control on the Reactor → master Fuel & Cooling → stock rods via the Plasma Chain → then take on the Fusion Reactor.
